Trail Physics · Unit 4: Energy & Momentum · Module 12

Momentum and Collisions

Momentum, impulse and conservation of momentum, and why stretching out a collision lowers the average force.

Lesson coming

The question

Why does bending your knees on a landing reduce the force you feel?

The physics

  • Momentum
  • Impulse
  • Impulse-momentum theorem
  • Conservation of momentum
  • Elastic and inelastic collisions

The math

  • p = mv
  • J = Δp = F_avg Δt

About the model: The Impact Lab uses hypothetical scenarios to teach impulse. It isn’t a way to judge protective gear or predict injury.

Learning objectives

  • Calculate momentum
  • Use the impulse-momentum theorem
  • Explain why a longer interaction time means a smaller average force
  • Use conservation of momentum in a collision
  • Tell elastic and inelastic collisions apart

Helps to know first: Newton’s Laws of Motion.

The mountain biking connection

Landing a jump or hitting a root changes a rider’s momentum. The same change spread over a longer time needs a smaller average force: impulse = force × time.
